## Learning objectives

Before the timed session, you should be able to open the prepared workshop
environment, load a verified copy of the teaching data, and prepare the dataset
versions used in the hands-on activities. You will use the same project,
dataset, and environment throughout the workshop.

Allow about 15 minutes, including startup time. Some familiarity with R is
helpful; you do not need previous experience with meta-analysis.

## Our teaching dataset

We use `HealthWellbeing` from the
[correlations chapter](https://doing-meta.guide/pooling-es#correlations)
[@harrer2021, sec. 4.2.4].
It contains study-level summaries of the association between health and
well-being. It is also distributed with the `dmetar` package.

The original review is @ngamaba2017. The dataset documentation describes
the variables [@healthwellbeing].

The workshop repository includes the authors' data file at
`data/raw/healthwellbeing.rda`, so you do not need to install `dmetar` or
download anything during the session. Keep the raw file unchanged and record
its source separately from any transformations you make later.

## Open the prepared environment {#choose-your-computing-environment}

Everyone uses the same prepared environment. MyBinder runs the workshop's
published image in your browser, with RStudio, R 4.4.1, Git, Quarto, and the
R packages recorded in the project lockfile already installed. There is nothing
to install during the workshop.

1. [Open RStudio on MyBinder](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r/HEAD?urlpath=rstudio)
   or use the link supplied by your instructor. Start it shortly before the
   workshop and keep the browser tab open; MyBinder stops idle sessions.
2. Once RStudio opens, use its **Terminal** for the project setup below.
   Run R commands and lesson exercises in the **Console** in the same browser
   session.
3. Download work you want to keep using **More → Export** in the RStudio
   **Files** pane. MyBinder sessions are temporary, and files in a session
   are lost when it ends.

If MyBinder fails to start, let the instructor know so you can use a prepared
alternative.

You can use your own computer instead, but complete the setup before the
workshop. Restore the project library with `renv::restore()` or use the
[Docker setup](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r#usage-with-docker).
On Linux, building the `dataspice` dependency `jqr` from source needs the jq
development library. Record your R version if it differs from 4.4.1.

## Get the project

Clone the project in the RStudio **Terminal**. If you have a GitHub account
and want to practise pushing changes after the workshop, use **Fork** on the
[workshop repository](https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r)
and replace `JBris` in the command with your GitHub username.

```bash
cd ~
git clone https://github.com/JBris/open-and-reproducible-science-in-r.git
cd open-and-reproducible-science-in-r
```

In RStudio’s **Files** pane, open the new `open-and-reproducible-science-in-r`
folder in your home directory and open `open-and-reproducible-science-in-r.Rproj`.
Keep Terminal and Console commands rooted in this project directory.

The project's `.Rprofile` activates renv. Check your R version and whether the
library matches the lockfile. If the library in your MyBinder session differs
from the lockfile, check with the instructor before proceeding.

```{r health-preparation-environment, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
R.version.string
renv::status()
```

## Verify the raw data {#preparation-data}

Run the following in the **R Console** from the project root. The R chunks
are also configured to run during rendering; setup chunks are uncached and
other R chunks use the cache.

The file is already in your project copy, so the download only runs if it is
missing. The checksum identifies the exact file used to prepare these lessons.
If you have a different copy, keep it and ask the instructor to resolve the
difference.

```{r health-preparation-download, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = TRUE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
raw_file <- file.path("data", "raw", "healthwellbeing.rda")
source_url <- paste0(
  "https://www.protectlab.org/meta-analysis-in-r/data/",
  "healthwellbeing.rda"
)

dir.create(dirname(raw_file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!file.exists(raw_file)) {
  download.file(source_url, destfile = raw_file, mode = "wb")
}

expected_md5 <- "0d74964b0b7168379a2b015cb648b326"
actual_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(raw_file))
stopifnot(identical(actual_md5, expected_md5))
actual_md5
```

Load into a separate environment so the file does not silently replace objects
in your working session. Use an explicit name for the dataset you will inspect.

```{r health-preparation-load, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = TRUE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
data_env <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
loaded_names <- load(raw_file, envir = data_env)
stopifnot(identical(loaded_names, "HealthWellbeing"))
health <- data_env[["HealthWellbeing"]]

expected_columns <- c("author", "cor", "n", "population", "country")
stopifnot(
  is.data.frame(health),
  nrow(health) == 29L,
  identical(names(health), expected_columns),
  !anyNA(health),
  all(is.finite(health$cor)),
  all(abs(health$cor) < 1),
  all(is.finite(health$n)),
  all(health$n > 3),
  all(health$n == floor(health$n))
)

head(health, 3)
dim(health)
```

Expected checkpoint: **29 rows and 5 columns**, with no assertion failures.
These checks describe this teaching snapshot, not a general rule that all
meta-analysis datasets must be complete or have this size.

## Prepare the dataset versions {#preparation-versions}

The hands-on activities read a specific, versioned copy of the dataset. Run the
prepared script once in the **Console**. It checks the raw file, stores two
versions on a local *pins* board, records their identifiers, and selects the
full dataset as the starting input for the pipeline.

```{r health-preparation-versions, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
source(file.path("pipelines", "prepare_health_wellbeing.R"))
```

Expected checkpoint: a table with two rows, `all` and `general`, each with a
version identifier. Identifiers record when a version was written, so yours
will differ from the instructor's. Running the script again reuses the same
versions. The instructor explains the board in the
[data and model versioning demonstration](04_versioning.qmd).

## Record the source

For your project notes, retain the book section, dataset documentation,
download URL, retrieval date, checksum, and original study citation. A package
licence or the workshop repository's MIT licence should not be assumed to
relicense every upstream dataset; check the relevant reuse terms before
redistributing data.

## Preparation checkpoint {#preparation-checkpoint}

You are ready when:

- RStudio is open in MyBinder, or in your own prepared setup, with the project
  open.
- You know your R version and `renv::status()` reports no problems.
- The raw file's checksum matches the teaching snapshot.
- The prepared script printed the `all` and `general` dataset versions.

Continue to the
[introduction, reproducibility principles, Git and GitHub](01_open_science.qmd).
